import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Some records are parts of a whole. A Brightwater booking holds its lines; a
client company holds its contacts. Facet models this as composition: the
parent owns its children, and the child cannot exist outside the parent. One
declaration on the parent and one on the child set the pair up.

## When to use this

Use composition when the child belongs to exactly one parent and dies with
it. Use a reference field when the target stands alone (see
[Link documents together](/build/model/relations/references-links/)) — a
ticket names its item, but the item exists before and after the ticket.

## Before you start

- **Both halves.** The parent declares a `children` entry, and the child
  declares `member_of` back. Facet rejects a one-sided pair.
- **Same domain, short name.** A child doctype lives in the same domain as
  its parent, and its name is written without the domain prefix.

## Steps

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the parent doctype in the **Builder** and tick **Aggregate root**.
2. Add a **Children** entry: a relationship name (for example `lines`), the
   child doctype, and the cardinality.
3. Open the child doctype, clear **Aggregate root**, and set **Member of**
   to the parent's name.
4. Publish — the check verifies the pair on both sides.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Files">

The Brightwater booking and its lines, exactly as the bundle ships them:

```yaml
# rentals/doctypes/rentals.Booking.yml (extract)
aggregate_root: true
children:
  lines:
    doctype: BookingLine
    collection: true
    description: "The equipment lines on this booking."

# rentals/doctypes/rentals.BookingLine.yml (extract)
aggregate_root: false
member_of: Booking
```

`collection: true` holds many children. A single-child relationship omits it.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Declare the child without a back-reference

Do not add a reference field on the child that points back at the parent.
Facet manages the parent link itself.

### Create the parent with its children in one call

Send a compound body: `$content` for the parent fields and `$children` for
the nested ones. Facet creates everything in one transaction. If one child
fails validation, nothing is written.

```sh
curl -k -X POST "https://facet.localhost:3443/Api/rentals/Booking" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FACET_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "$content": { "client": "clients.Company.06H1FM1B3MXBPS0JYVM3BDD154", "dates": { "start": "2026-12-07", "end": "2026-12-09" } },
    "$children": {
      "lines": [ { "item": "equipment.Item.EQ-2026-0001", "quantity": 2, "price": { "value": "250.00", "currency": "EUR" } } ]
    }
  }'
```

`-k` skips the certificate check of the local development address. The
response carries the parent and the created children; the line takes its
field defaults. In the app, the parent's document page creates and lists the
children on their own tabs.

## The rules composition gives you

| Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Cascade delete | Deleting the parent deletes its children. |
| Lock coupling | A write to a child locks the parent, so the aggregate stays consistent. |
| Flat create refused | A child created outside its parent answers `422`. Use the nested route. |
| Inherited access | A permission on the parent covers the child, because the child path extends the parent path. |
| Event fan-out | A child change notifies the parent, so parent-side computed fields update. |

{/* d2
*One aggregate: the parent owns its lines*
parent: "Booking (aggregate root)" {class: node}
line1: "BookingLine" {class: node}
line2: "BookingLine" {class: node}
delete: "Delete the booking" {class: external}

parent -> line1: owns
parent -> line2: owns
delete -> parent: cascades down
*/}
<div class="d2-diagram">
<img class="d2-diagram__img d2-diagram__light" src="/diagrams/0bf532da-light.svg" alt="Booking (aggregate root)" loading="lazy" />
<img class="d2-diagram__img d2-diagram__dark" src="/diagrams/0bf532da-dark.svg" alt="Booking (aggregate root)" loading="lazy" />
</div>

The cascade runs downward only: deleting a child never deletes the parent.

## Troubleshooting

### Publish refuses the pair

One half of the composition is missing. Add the `member_of` on the child or
the `children` entry on the parent, then publish again.

### A flat create of the child answers `422`

Children are created through the parent. Use the nested route on the parent
document, or the compound body shown above.

### The child shows under a different parent after a copy

It cannot. A copy re-parents the child to the copied parent, never to the
original one.

### A reference field would be simpler

If the child has a life outside the parent — several parents, its own
access rule, its own list page — model it as an aggregate root with a
reference field instead. See
[Link documents together](/build/model/relations/references-links/).
